newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli ministerial panel to meet on privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Israeli ministerial panel to meet on privatisation.

text.p: The Israeli ministerial privatisation committee will meet on Wednesday evening to discuss a plan for selling off state enterprises, the prime minister's office said on Tuesday.

The three-man committee, which consists of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Finance Minister Dan Meridor and Justice Minister Tzahi Henegbi, is empowered to make all final decisions on privatisation.
Officials would not say whether the committee would approve the plan or simply discuss it.

The government had promised to unveil the plan as early as last October. It has not released any details, but the plan is believed to call for selling shares in Israel Chemicals Ltd, Bezeq Israel Telecom and Zim Israel Navigation.
In addition, the Treasury is seeking to sell stakes by tender or by floating shares in three or four of the commercial banks.
In December, Moshe Leon, Netanyahu's adviser on economic policy, said the privatisation plan consisted of a list of companies to be privatised but gave no further details.
